text:
jamie: Heads up — customer onprem deploy reported a bastion cert rotation that triggered KMS key expiration warnings. They also have an attestation step that fails if the bastion identity changes. Anyone seen this combo before?
morgan: ouch. do we have an official recommendation for bastion key lifecycle in Private? I thought we pinned keystore+attestation to host-id.
riley: we do, but the customer is using short-lived keys via their KMS shim (30d). bastion cert renewed -> identity hash changed -> attestation fails.
sasha: TL;DR: need to decouple instance identity for attestation vs. TLS cert lifetime. attestation should use the instance fingerprint uploaded at install, not the ephemeral cert.
jamie: exactly. customer asked whether rolling keys should be allowed without disrupting audit pairing. they want to rotate every 30d for compliance.
dave: safe approach: keep KMS DEK stable for storage of identity blob; rotate KEK (wrapping key) frequently. that way stored attestation values decrypt unchanged.
morgan: can we support that with our current onprem agent? agent stores identity in /var/lib/redwood/attest.json encrypted with local DEK currently derived from KMS.
riley: current agent: derivation -> fetch KMS key -> unwrap DEK. If KMS key rotates, unwrap still works if key versioning keeps old key versions for unwrap. question is whether customers keep prior key versions for long enough.
sasha: we should add doc & probe that verifies unwrap across key versions. also add a fallback to cached wrapped-DEK for N hours if KMS unavailable during rotation.
security-bot: [audit] note: any change to key usage must be logged to audit sink with fields: actor, key_id, operation, key_version, container_id.
jamie: audit sink — customer wants to forward audit logs to their SIEM (Splunk). Our onprem agent currently writes to local journal and optional s3-compatible blob. How to forward securely?
morgan: we can add an encrypted forwarder that posts to customer endpoint over mTLS. config knobs: forwarder.enabled, forwarder.endpoint, forwarder.client_cert_path.
riley: for quick mitigation, suggest they enable local-forwarder -> push to their proxy that does batching. Also ensure we redact secrets (no raw KMS tokens) before sending.
dave: network policy note: bastion must NOT have egress to the public internet except to KMS endpoints and artifact registry. enforce via iptables/netpol and verify with a daily egress-scan.
sasha: vulnerability triage: if bastion egress was open at time of rotation, attacker could exfiltrate identity blob. playbook: 1) revoke KMS KEK immediately; 2) rotate DEK and rewrap; 3) invalidate prior attestation tokens; 4) run host forensic capture.
jamie: do we have automated tooling to revoke and rewrap on a fleet? customer size ~30 hosts.
riley: not fully automated for onprem fleets; we have a cli: redwood-agent rewrap --host <id> --new-kek <key-id>. we should add a bulk mode and a canary rollout with health-check.
morgan: +1. also surface a safe mode where we keep one host pinned to old KEK during rollout so attestation doesn't break service.
security-bot: [incident] when you revoke keys, create audit ticket and ping #eng-security-incidents with tags: onprem, kms, bastion, high-prio.
dave: RBAC change: we'll need a temporary role (attest-rotate) scoped to key rewrap + audit.log: write-only. propose we add a short-lived role in IAM and a script to request it with approval flow.
sasha: add unit: 'rotation-approver' that requires two approvers for KEK revoke. store approvals in audit log.
jamie: I'll draft a runbook: steps + commands + SLA times. rough SLA ideas: detect rotation anomaly -> 15m ack -> 60m revoke KEK if suspicious -> 4h full fleet rewrap.
riley: include checklist: collect /var/log/attest*, netstat, iptables-save, agent version, KMS key versions.
morgan: I'll prototype the bulk rewrap CLI and a dry-run flag. aim to demo tomorrow EOD.
jamie: awesome. can someone capture a minimal config snippet for forwarder and RBAC role so I can add to the runbook?
sasha: pasteme:

```
forwarder:
  enabled: true
  endpoint: https://logs.example.local/ingest
  client_cert: /etc/redwood/mtls.crt
  redact_fields: ["kms_token","raw_dek"]
```

and RBAC example:

```
role: attest-rotate
permissions:
  - kms:RewrapKey
  - audit:Write
scope: hosts: [tag:private-onprem]
max_duration: 1h
```

security-bot: [reminder] file the runbook PR to repos/ops/onprem/attestation-runbooks within 24h.
jamie: thanks all — filing PR now. tagging @morgan for the CLI demo. i'll also ping customer with short timeline and temporary mitigations (disable public egress, enable forwarder).
morgan: on it :thumbsup: 
riley: will add the egress-scan to daily checks and create a simple netpol template for kube and iptables snippet for non-kube hosts.
jamie: closing loop — will update thread with runbook link + incident ticket once PR merged.
